subject: Borealis private pool sizing — lane allocations, egress plan, and throughput proforma
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily@borealisai.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@borealisai.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: private GPU pool sizing for Borealis on-prem deployment

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Borealis is ready to move forward with a private deployment (VPC-connected, on-prem GPU pool) for our inference workloads. We need a sizing and performance plan we can review with our infra and procurement teams next week. Key asks:

- Target sustained throughput: approx 1.8M tokens/day (~average request 200 tokens) with burst headroom up to ~3x for promos.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 300ms for the latency-sensitive lane.
- Cost preference: prefer lower-cost throughput lane for batch/analytics-style traffic.
- Network constraints: our colo has a 12 Gbps cross-connect to the cloud; egress costs are a concern.
- Compliance: audit logs + short-term retention for debug traces.

Can your team put together a short proforma: GPU counts, lane allocations (low-latency vs throughput), autoscale policy suggestions, and an egress/egress-mitigation plan (caching/edge). Please include a rough timeline for deployment (pilot -> staging -> prod).

We have a kickoff with infra + procurement on Oct 15; would appreciate a draft before then.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Platform Engineering
Borealis AI

[Attachment: current-traffic-sample.csv (csv)]

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff: private GPU pool sizing for Borealis on-prem deployment

Emily — thanks, this is exactly the right level of detail. I pulled together a first-pass sizing/proforma and lane allocation that addresses throughput, latency, and egress. Dropping the high-level summary here and attaching the workbook with the modeling. Jonas and Vivek — please flag anything I missed.

Summary (first-pass):
- Workload assumptions: avg request = 200 tokens; peak traffic window = 30 mins/day with 3x baseline.
- Target sustained: ~1.8M tokens/day ≈ 9,000 avg requests/day (≈6 requests/minute sustained; peaks to ~18 requests/minute).
- Latency lane (low-latency): target 95p <= 300ms, use smaller batch sizes (1-4), dedicate ~25% of capacity to this lane, prefer larger instance types with NVLink for smaller batch jitter reduction.
- Throughput lane (cost-optimized): larger batching (batch 16-64), 75% of capacity, aggressive KV/prefix caching and long-lived inference workers.
- Per-GPU assumptions (conservative): baseline single GPU effective throughput = ~1,400 tokens/sec (mixed quantized model variant), with batching this can increase to ~3,500 tokens/sec in throughput lane.
- Baseline GPU count (pilot): 6 GPUs (2 dedicated to latency lane equivalently apportioned as 25% of total). Prod baseline: 18 GPUs to meet sustained with burst cushion; autoscale up to 30 GPUs for peak 3x bursts.
- Warm pool: keep ~20% idle-warm (cold-to-ready transition ~30–60s depending on model and KV warmup).
- Network egress: estimate 0.9 TB/day (model responses only) → ~27 TB/month; suggest edge caching for repeated outputs and token compression where possible. Also recommend negotiated egress cap with the colo or routing through a worn Egress Bucket with daily alerts.
- Failover: automatic fallback to a quantized variant routed to the throughput lane if latency lane is saturated.

Attachments: borealis_throughput_model_v1.xlsx (workbook), lane-allocation-diagram.png, network-egress-budget.pdf

Next steps / requested from Borealis:
1) Confirm expected peak window (time-of-day and duration) and any synchronous SLAs for specific endpoints (owner: Emily / due: Oct 14).
2) Provide sample traffic histogram (burstiness) / session affinity constraints (owner: Rajiv / due: Oct 14).
3) Approve pilot scope (6 GPUs) so we can schedule pilot rollout in your staging rack.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the proforma tomorrow.

—Chloe

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: private GPU pool sizing for Borealis on-prem deployment (technical notes)

Chloe — good draft. A few technical clarifications / conservative adjustments we should include in the proforma before sending to Borealis:

1) Per-GPU performance and effective capacity modeling
   - Use two model variants in estimates: full-precision (FP16/fused) and quantized (4-bit QKV-friendly) as fallback.
   - Conservative throughput numbers per 80GB-class GPU:
     * Latency lane (batch 1–4): ~400–700 tokens/sec effective per GPU (higher latency penalty due to small batches and attention overhead).
     * Throughput lane (batch 16–64): ~2,500–3,500 tokens/sec per GPU depending on request length and model size.
   - For sizing, use latency-lane baseline 500 t/s and throughput-lane 2,800 t/s to avoid underprovisioning.

2) Mapping tokens -> requests for autoscale math
   - With avg 200 tokens/request: 1 GPU in throughput lane (2,800 t/s) ≈ 14 requests/sec ≈ 50k req/hour. Convert to daily sustained: ~1.7M tokens/day per GPU at steady rates (confirm with workbook).

3) Autoscale & admission control
   - Recommend two thresholds: target utilization 60% for steady-state autoscale, emergency threshold 90% to trigger spillover/fallback.
   - Warm pool sizing: maintain 15–25% warm to hit 95p latency on short-notice spikes. Warm-up time dominated by KV cache: ~20–45s in best-case with pre-warmed prefixes.

4) Networking & egress mitigation
   - Given 12 Gbps cross-connect, sustained egress for model responses is safe, but spikes during bulk export/analytics must be rate-limited.
   - Propose an egress token compressor service at edge (gzip-like payload reduction + structured output delta encoding) and per-customer daily egress cap with alerts in the Console.

5) Operational runbook items to include in deliverable:
   - Canary deploy steps for model variants, circuit-breaker thresholds, step-down rollback plan.
   - Runbook for cold-start incidents (repopulate KV, restart long-lived workers).

Action: I'll update the workbook assumptions with the conservative per-GPU numbers (500 / 2800) and add autoscale thresholds. Chloe, once updated we should run the numbers to translate to the 18 GPU prod projection and confirm monthly egress.

—Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff: private GPU pool sizing for Borealis on-prem deployment — updated proforma & next steps

Emily / Rajiv — attached is the updated proforma and a short runbook that incorporates Jonas's conservative numbers and the autoscale/admission controls we discussed. High-level changes:

- Per-GPU conservative assumptions: latency lane = 500 t/s, throughput lane = 2,800 t/s.
- Revised baseline counts: pilot = 6 GPUs (2 latency / 4 throughput), prod baseline = 20 GPUs (5 latency / 15 throughput) to hit sustained 1.8M tokens/day with 30% headroom; autoscale cap = 32 GPUs for 3x bursts.
- Autoscale policy: scale when 5-minute moving avg utilization > 60%; scale down when < 40% for 10 minutes. Emergency spillover at 90% util → route to quantized throughput lane or reject non-critical requests.
- Warm-pool recommendation: 20% of total GPUs warm (preloaded KV), expected cold-to-ready ~30–45s for the models we tested.
- Egress: estimate ~27 TB/month if no compression; with edge compression + response dedupe we project ~12–15 TB/month. Recommend negotiating colo egress tiers and adding daily egress alerts in Redwood Console.

Action items (owners & timing):
- Emily / Rajiv: confirm peak window & any synchronous endpoint SLAs (due 2026-10-14).
- Borealis infra: share traffic histogram (hourly) and any session stickiness constraints (due 2026-10-14).
- Redwood (Jonas + Vivek): finalize pilot runbook and provisioning checklist for staging rack (due 2026-10-14).
- Chloe: book 30-min walkthrough with Borealis Oct 14 or Oct 15 (I'll propose times).

If these numbers look reasonable, we'll convert the workbook into a short slide set for your procurement and infra meeting on Oct 15.

Thanks — looking forward.

—Chloe
